subject: mathematics
question_text: In a △ABC, prove that cot(A/2) + cot(B/2) + cot(C/2) = s²/Δ.

mark_split.label: Write each cotangent as a standard form

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each standard result you use and the order you use them in.

steps.label: Write each cotangent as a standard form
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. cot(A/2) = s(s−a)/Δ is a standard result — quote it rather than deriving it. All three terms then share s/Δ.

recall.must_convey: That cot(A/2) = s(s−a)/Δ is used for each term and s/Δ taken out as a common factor.
accept: cot half A is s into s minus a over delta and the three share s over delta
write each cotangent in the standard form and factor
take s over delta common from the three terms
cot half A ante s into s minus a by delta
use the standard cot half angle result

steps.why: All three cotangents have the same shape, so factoring s/Δ out immediately leaves only the brackets to add.
common_mistakes: Using cot A instead of cot(A/2).
Forgetting the s in the numerator.

steps.label: Add the brackets and conclude
steps.margin_note: The other half. (s−a) + (s−b) + (s−c) is 3s − (a+b+c), and a+b+c is 2s — so the brackets collapse to s.

recall.must_convey: That the brackets add to 3s − 2s = s, giving s²/Δ.
accept: the brackets give three s minus two s which is s so it becomes s squared over delta
a plus b plus c is two s so three s minus two s leaves s
the answer is s squared over delta
three s minus two s equals s, so s square by delta

steps.why: a + b + c = 2s by definition of the semi-perimeter. Writing s instead of 2s is the single commonest error in this whole unit.
common_mistakes: Writing a + b + c = s and getting 2s²/Δ.
